title: Flatness survives restriction to a slice
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site, let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal C$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a flat $\mathcal O$-module [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Then the restriction $\mathcal F|_U$ is a flat $\mathcal O_U$-module on the slice site over $U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

proof.text: Take an arbitrary exact three-term complex $\mathcal G_1\to\mathcal G_2\to\mathcal G_3$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules. Write $j_{U!}$ for the sheafified direct-sum extension of the cited exactness lemma. Its forward implication gives an exact complex $j_{U!}\mathcal G_1\to j_{U!}\mathcal G_2\to j_{U!}\mathcal G_3$ of $\mathcal O$-modules.

Flatness of $\mathcal F$ means precisely that the functor $\mathcal H\mapsto\mathcal H\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal F$ is exact. Apply that hypothesis to the complex in step 1: $(j_{U!}\mathcal G_1)\otimes\mathcal F\to(j_{U!}\mathcal G_2)\otimes\mathcal F\to(j_{U!}\mathcal G_3)\otimes\mathcal F$ is exact.

For $i=1,2,3$ use the natural isomorphism $j_{U!}(\mathcal G_i\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}\mathcal F|_U)\cong(j_{U!}\mathcal G_i)\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal F$. Naturality in $\mathcal G_i$ identifies each arrow induced by $a:\mathcal G_i\to\mathcal G_{i+1}$: the isomorphism at $i+1$ composed with $j_{U!}(a\otimes1)$ equals $(j_{U!}a\otimes1)$ composed with the isomorphism at $i$. Thus the complex in step 2 is isomorphic to the extension by zero of the tensor complex on the slice, and the latter extended complex is exact.

Apply the reverse implication of the exactness lemma to conclude that $\mathcal G_1\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}\mathcal F|_U\to\mathcal G_2\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}\mathcal F|_U\to\mathcal G_3\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}\mathcal F|_U$ is exact. The original complex was arbitrary, including those with a zero end term, so tensoring with $\mathcal F|_U$ is exact. By the definition of flatness on $(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal O_U)$ this is the conclusion.
